title: Justification opposed to condemnation
source_text: V. Sed maxime manifesta est ista vocis hujus acceptio in locis illis in quibus justificatio opponitur condemnationi. Cujus rei exemplum habemus Prov. 17. Qui justificat impium, & qui condemnat justum, abominabilis est uterque apud Deum; & Matth. 12. Per verba tua justificaberis, & per verba tua condemnaberis. Quibus jungi potest illud Jobi cap. 9. Si memet justifico, meum ipsius os me condemnabit.
pass_a_gloss: But most manifest is this acceptation of the word in those places in which justification is opposed to condemnation. Of which matter we have an example in Prov. 17: He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the just, both are abominable before God; and Matt. 12: By thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned. To which can be joined that of Job chapter 9: If I justify myself, my own mouth will condemn me.
pass_b_english: Clearest forensic use: justification set against condemnation (Prov 17; Matt 12).
Job 9: self-justification still meets the mouth's condemnation.
